terms.gloss: ownership, the right of an owner
evidence: Liv. 45.13.15: dominium et jūs eōrum quī dederint esse (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The lawyers’ word for full ownership, as against possessiō, mere holding (Gai. Inst. 2.7). In speech Latin asks whose a thing is: cujus est?, and answers meum est (see own).
Having and occupying a thing, whether or not one owns it in law; also the thing held, an estate (see property).
In Cicero a thing’s own nature, its peculiar quality; ownership only after Augustus (Suet., Dig.).

phrases.latin: nūllīus bonī sine sociō jūcunda possessiō est
phrases.english: no good thing is a pleasure to own without someone to share it

sources: Lewis & Short: dominium · Lewis & Short: possessio · Lewis & Short: proprietas
